_comment: One entry per Tool registered on Cleo's agent in Relevance AI. Field names here (title, description, method, url, headers, params) match Relevance AI's HTTP/API Tool step as of this design — check the current Relevance AI docs when you actually create these, since exact field names shift between UI versions. What matters structurally: each tool's `description` is the ONLY thing the LLM sees to decide when to call it, so it must say what the tool does and when to use it, not just its name. `{{secrets.BOLT_TOOL_SECRET}}` and `{{secrets.BOLT_BACKEND_URL}}` are Relevance AI's Custom API Key templating (Integrations & API Keys -> Custom API Keys in the Relevance AI UI) — store both there once and every tool below references them, so nothing is hardcoded per tool.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.title: Get dataset profile
tools.description: Returns a deterministic column-by-column profile of the dataset: inferred type, null percentage, unique percentage, and a formatting-issue count per column. Call this first, before proposing anything, to see what the dataset actually contains.

tools.name: run_validator
tools.title: Run deterministic validation rules
tools.description: Runs the fixed set of deterministic cleaning rules (state code normalization, email format cleanup, phone E.164 normalization, categorical canonicalization) against a dataset and returns every violation found, each with the rule name, affected column, row count, and a small before/after sample. This is your evidence — cite it, don't restate it from memory.

column.description: Optional — limit the scan to one column.

tools.name: get_diff_preview
tools.title: Preview a rule's before/after diff
tools.description: Re-runs a single named rule against one column and returns a fresh before/after sample, without changing any data. Use this to confirm or refresh evidence for a specific recommendation before writing your explanation, especially if the dataset may have changed since run_validator last ran.

tools.name: write_audit_log
tools.title: Write an audit log entry
tools.description: Appends an entry to the immutable audit trail — call this for your own reasoning milestones (e.g. after profiling, after proposing a recommendation) so there is a record of what you did and when, separate from the approval/execution entries Bolt writes on its own.

tools.name: check_job_status
tools.title: Check a job's status
tools.description: Returns the current status (queued/running/awaiting_approval/completed/failed) and progress percentage of a profiling/cleaning job. Use this if a run needs to check whether earlier work on the same dataset has finished.

tools.name: execute_rules_engine
tools.title: Execute a cleaning rule (GATED)
tools.description: Applies a specific rule to a column, permanently modifying the dataset. This ONLY succeeds if a human has already approved the exact recommendationId in the Bolt UI — otherwise it returns { error: "denied" } and nothing changes. Only call this after a recommendation has been presented and you have reason to believe it was approved (e.g. the workflow explicitly tells you it was); never call it speculatively or to 'try' whether something is approved.

recommendationId.description: Must match the id a human approved in the UI.

tools.name: save_workflow
tools.title: Save a reusable workflow (GATED)
tools.description: Registers a named, reusable combination of rules in the Workflow Registry for future runs. Like execute_rules_engine, this ONLY succeeds if the associated recommendationId has already been approved by a human — otherwise it returns { error: "denied" }.
